title: gpui-status never written: --hyphen flags never construct RuntimeHostBridge
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hq-status-zero-root-cause (high)
gpui-status never written: hub launched with --hyphen flags the parser stores as 'runtime-host' keys, so RuntimeHostBridge is never constructed (silent None) and zero status writes ever run

C++: Retail C++ accepts only exact single-dash tokens: WinMain.cpp:892-920 tokenizes lpCmdLine via nextParam and matches whole tokens with stricmp, e.g. WinMain.cpp:903 `if (stricmp(token,"-win")==0) ApplicationIsWindowed=true;`. A GNU-style `--runtime-host=windowed` token has no C++ parsing path at all.

Rust: hub describe windowed-generals (failed exit=1 uptime=2m15s, matching brief pid 81341 / ~2m15s): `generals --runtime-host=windowed --windowed ... --gpui-control=/tmp/generals_windowed_control.txt --gpui-status=/tmp/generals_windowed_status.txt --gpui-frame=/tmp/generals_windowed_frame.png`. command_line.rs:338 `let option_name = arg.trim_start_matches('-');` strips dashes but the equals-split at :341-345 keeps the inner hyphen, inserting options key `"runtime-host"`/`"gpui-status"` (generic insert at :112). get_option_value (command_line.rs:531-534) lowercases only — no hyphen→underscore normalization. Consumers use underscore keys: option_takes_value list command_line.rs:397-402 (`runtime_host|gpui_control|gpui_status|gpui_frame`); RuntimeHostBridge::is_runtime_host_requested runtime.rs:218-222 and from_command_line runtime.rs:226-231 (`args.get_option_value("gpui_control")?` etc.). Resu

Fix: Launch with the underscore single-dash form the code and the smoke harness use — exactly executable_smoke.rs:967-978: `-runtime_host=windowed -windowed -gpui_control=… -gpui_status=… -gpui_frame=…`. Durable fix: in CommandLineArgs::parse_option (command_line.rs:343,348) normalize the option name via name.replace('-', "_") (or match both spellings like the existing `"smoke-test"|"smoketest"` alias at command_line.rs:~285), and make RuntimeHostBridge::from_command_line log a warning when `runtime_

### hq-status-write-not-frame-gated (medium)
Answer to the gating question: the status write is NOT gated on a frame that never happens — publish_booting runs synchronously before the event loop, so the hang cannot explain 0 bytes; only bridge-never-constructed can

C++: C++ GameEngine::execute main loop (GameEngine.cpp, m_maxFPS limit ~:856) always returns control to the OS pump each frame; there is no file-status publish in C++ to compare, so the relevant C++ fact is that the WinMain pump (WinMain.cpp:965+) keeps running while frames render — a hung frame would still leave earlier-published observable state.

Rust: run_loop.rs:66-69: `RuntimeHostBridge::from_command_line(...)` then `bridge.publish_booting()` execute synchronously BEFORE `event_loop.run(...)` (run_loop.rs:~88) — not frame-gated. run_loop.rs:322-326 publishes again via publish_booting_from_winit_query immediately after window creation. Per-frame publish_runtime sits at the END of drive_frame (run_loop.rs:282-285) → publish_status → unconditional `let _ = fs::write(&self.status_path, payload)` (runtime.rs, end of publish_status). Therefore a mid-frame hang (macOS 'not responding' = winit closure stuck inside engine.update/render) would freeze updates but leave the LAST payload on disk — proven by the earlier 16:07 run where the same file held `state=Menu ui_screen=Some(MainMenu) fps=30 frame=8374` (session transcript findearthmap_art.jsonl line 287). A 0-byte file requires zero publishes ever — consistent only with bridge None.

Fix: No engine fix needed for the 0 bytes itself; for diagnosis, publish_booting could include the parsed runtime_host/gpui option spellings so a misconfigured launch is visible as state=Booting with an args-mismatch field.
close_reason: Hyphen --runtime-host/--gpui-status aliases construct RuntimeHostBridge. test_hyphen_runtime_host_aliases_resolve + hyphen_runtime_host_flags_construct_bridge pass.

title: Unbounded waypoint chain walks hang Menu after ScriptEngine first update
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hang-01 (high)
Hang frame identified: everything after 'ScriptEngine first update' runs in ONE unbounded-duration logic frame; update_shell_with_budget(dt,1) bounds frame COUNT not TIME — C++ GAME_SHELL ticks bounded subsystems on the main loop

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/System/GameLogic.cpp:3600-3602 — TheScriptEngine->UPDATE() runs inline in GameLogic::update on the main logic loop; every pass there (scripts, terrain, modules, AI, partition, destroy list) is bounded per frame, and camera waypoint setup is capped at 25 (W3DView.cpp:2835, W3DView.h:28), so GAME_SHELL never blocks the UI.

Rust: Log fires at the START of crate ScriptEngine::update_active (GameLogic/src/scripting/engine/update.rs:41-52). Same-frame remainder: execute_side_scripts over 10 sides x 82 scripts (update.rs:124-243), team-factory update, sequential progression, then Main's SECOND walker mission_scripts.update (Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:361-373), the drain block (scripts_camera.rs:423-660), then terrain/water-edge/process_commands/sleepy Movement->host pathfinding (Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/step.rs:131-260). Entry camera_drain.rs:291-293 host_update_shell_with_budget(dt,1) -> step.rs:54-104: the budget limits fixed steps per present, NOT the duration of one update_simulation. shell.rs:1819-1823 already documents a prior minutes-long single step ('pathfinding/scripts + ASSET_MANAGER'). No info log exists between the first-update log and the next warns ('Slow mission script u

Fix: Add per-phase timing/watchdog logging inside evaluate_and_execute_scripts and update_simulation phases so a hung shell frame names its phase; optionally a frame-time abort guard. Do not implement per assignment.

### hang-02 (high)
ScriptCameraPathMove::new walks waypoint link[0] chain with NO bound — infinite loop + unbounded Vec on cyclic/bi-directional paths; C++ caps at MAX_WAYPOINTS=25

C++: W3DView.cpp:2835 'while (pWay && m_mcwpInfo.numWaypoints < MAX_WAYPOINTS)' with W3DView.h:28 'enum {MAX_WAYPOINTS=25};' — chain walk hard-capped. C++ builds the same cyclic graph incl. bi-directional reverse links (TerrainLogic.cpp:1374-1384).

Rust: Main/src/game_logic/game_logic/script_camera.rs:201-208 — 'while let Some(next_id) = current.get_link(0) { ... points.push(...); current = next; }' with no cap or visited-set; reverse links created at GameLogic/src/terrain.rs:2306-2329 (add_waypoint_link). MAP DATA (I RefPack-decoded ShellMapMD.map via a JS port of script_loader.rs decompress_refpack_stream): 139 waypoints, 114 links, 34 waypoints start CYCLIC link[0] chains (Car_Path 17-ring, Chinook_Path 4-ring, Hover_Path1/2, Commanche_Patrol). NOT the observed shell hang: ShellMapMD has ZERO MOVE_CAMERA_ALONG_WAYPOINT_PATH actions (rawType 17 count 0; camera uses rawType 14 MoveCameraTo, bounded) — but any map whose scripts use that action into a cyclic chain hangs forever while C++ stops at 25.

Fix: Port the C++ bound: stop at 25 waypoints or track visited ids; keep partial-chain semantics on dangling links. Do not implement per assignment.

### hang-03 (high)
UnitAIUpdate FollowWaypointPath chain walk unbounded except a >1-link break — cyclic 1-link rings (ShellMapMD Car_Path) loop forever; C++ caps unit waypoint queue at 16

C++: AIUpdate.h:681-683 'enum { MAX_WAYPOINTS = 16 }; Coord3D m_waypointQueue[MAX_WAYPOINTS]' + AIUpdate.cpp:1141 'if (m_waypointCount < MAX_WAYPOINTS)' — unit waypoint queues length-capped.

Rust: GameLogic/src/object/unit/ai_commands.rs:1341-1351 — builds 'chain' via 'while let Some(node) = current { chain.push(...); if node.get_num_links() > 1 { break; } current = node.get_link(0)... }'. Decoded ShellMapMD: Car_Path/Chinook_Path/Hover rings have exactly ONE outgoing link per node -> walk never terminates, 'chain' grows unboundedly. Issued by do_team_follow_waypoints (executor/actions_victory_team.rs:376-421) / do_named_follow_waypoints (actions_named.rs:90-136); the shell patrol scripts target exactly these rings ('Chinooks Patrol' rawType 36 Chinook_Path, 'Hover Patrol' rawType 56 Hover_Path1, 'Spawn Trucks And Attack' rawType 113 Van_Path). Currently no-op on the live host (empty OBJECT_REGISTRY dual-world) but a latent deterministic hang once crate objects/teams are populated.

Fix: Cap the walk at 16 (AIUpdate MAX_WAYPOINTS) or break on revisit. Do not implement per assignment.
close_reason: TerrainLogic::walk_link0_chain visited-set + WAYPOINT_PATH_LIMIT=1024. ScriptCameraPathMove and UnitAI fallback use it. Cyclic Car_Path cannot unbounded-grow.

title: Sync W3D+texture loads on render thread; no negative cache; beachball
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hang-1 (critical)
CONFIRMED: Live render path performs synchronous W3D loads on the main (render) thread, re-attempted every frame for missing models — render-thread sync-load hang is real

C++: C++ never loads geometry during the frame draw: (1) all condition-state models are preloaded at map load behind the loading screen — W3DModelDraw.cpp:1099 W3DModelDrawModuleData::preloadAssets → :363 ModelConditionInfo::preloadAssets → W3DDisplay.cpp:3195-3207 W3DDisplay::preloadModelAssets → Load_3D_Assets("name.w3d"), and W3DAssetManager.cpp:966-999 Load_3D_Assets early-returns 'this file has already been loaded' from a loaded-files hash so a miss is attempted once per file, never per frame; (2) render objects are persistent per drawable condition state (W3DModelDraw.cpp:3010 m_renderObject = Create_Render_Obj(...) once on state change), the per-frame draw never re-resolves; (3) textures stream on a dedicated background thread — textureloader.cpp:181-205 LoaderThreadClass _TextureLoadThread ('Texture loader thread', priority -4) with _ForegroundQueue/_BackgroundQueue, main thread only 

Rust: run_loop.rs:79-203: winit event_loop.run closure → drive_frame → engine.render() executes on the macOS main thread; blocking it starves AppKit → beachball. Inside render(): input.rs:1377-1382 computes deferred budget and allow_sync_model_loads; pipeline_execute.rs:161-179 collect_render_items → pipeline_collect.rs:919-1093 ensure_render_model_loaded runs INLINE in the frame: locks the global asset manager, calls sync load_w3d_model (manager.rs:2009-2084; block_in_place/block_on when multithread runtime), and on failure falls to resolve_mesh_for_model_key (mesh_asset_resolve.rs:1240-1330) which re-locks the manager and probes up to 4 candidate keys, then try_load_w3d_from_filesystem → find_filesystem_w3d. RenderModelLoadResult::Failed is never cached anywhere (pipeline_collect.rs:624-637 just counts it) and render items are rebuilt statelessly every frame — so every missing model is re-at

Fix: Mirror C++ structure: preload all condition-state models at map/shell load (W3DDisplay::preloadModelAssets analog) with a per-file attempted-once cache, cache negative results (pipeline-level failed-key set mirroring C++ LoadedFiles + HAnimManager.Is_Missing), and make render-time resolution cache-only (fail to no-draw like C++ NULL robj) instead of sync I/O per item per frame.

### hang-2 (critical)
Residual filesystem W3D walk has NO negative cache: ~700-1000 stat'd candidate paths rebuilt and re-stat'd per missing model per frame (the actual per-frame wall)

C++: W3DAssetManager.cpp:966-999: Load_3D_Assets checks the loaded-files hash first and returns TRUE ('this file has already been loaded') — a failed or successful file load is never re-read; assetmgr.cpp:906-908 HAnimManager.Is_Missing(name) skips repeat on-demand loads of known-missing animations; C++ has no per-frame filesystem directory probing at all — asset paths are resolved through the mounted BIG archives and the loaded-files hash.

Rust: mesh_asset_resolve.rs:51-60 W3D_SEARCH_ROOT_RESIDUALS has 9 entries; :919-946 w3d_filename_variants produces ~12 case/casing variants per key; :955-1002 filesystem_w3d_candidates joins ~28 roots (cwd + 9 residuals + 4 cwd-relative + 5 manifest-relative + 9 manifest-../../../ residuals) × filenames × {root, Art/W3D, art/w3d} ≈ 700-1000 PathBufs with a dedup HashSet, and find_filesystem_w3d (:1022-1026) stat's each via is_file(). try_load_w3d_from_filesystem (:1134-1155) is reached from resolve_mesh_for_model_key on EVERY load attempt for a missing model. The AssetManager negative cache missing_model_keys (manager.rs:2025-2033) only guards the archive probe inside load_w3d_model — nothing guards this walk. For a 271-missing-model scene this is ~200k-270k stats + equivalent allocations per frame on the render thread.

Fix: Add a process-wide negative cache keyed by canonical model key that gates resolve_mesh_for_model_key entirely (record on first Missing result, like manager.rs missing_model_keys but covering the residual path), and/or build the root list once as a static — C++ parity is one attempted lookup per file identity, not per frame.

### hang-3 (critical)
Startup deferral budget is bypassed: RenderBridge drain hardcodes allow_sync_model_loads=true, and any non-Menu state (or missing startup anchor) sets budget=0 → unbounded sync loads for ALL items every frame

C++: C++ has no per-frame load budget because it has no per-frame loading — preloadAssets (W3DModelDraw.cpp:1099) covers every drawable's condition states at map load once, and Create_Render_Obj results persist in m_renderObject (W3DModelDraw.cpp:3010). On-demand loading (assetmgr.cpp:728) exists but the persistent-robj design means it fires on state change, not per frame.

Rust: shell.rs:767-791 startup_deferred_model_load_budget returns 0 whenever current_state != Menu or startup_frame is None → input.rs:1382 allow_sync_model_loads = (budget == 0) is then TRUE and pipeline_execute.rs:146-155 sets deferred_model_load_budget = usize::MAX — every render item sync-loads per frame (also triggers prewarm_startup_models, pipeline_execute.rs:127-137). Worse, even inside Menu the GameClient drawable path bypasses the budget entirely: pipeline_execute.rs:210-216 calls drain_render_bridge_submissions, and pipeline_collect.rs:1301-1309 calls ensure_render_model_loaded(graphics_system, model_name, model_name, TRUE, budget) with hardcoded allow_sync=true — every bridge submission (shell-map scenery drawables) gets an uncapped sync load attempt every frame. This is the unbounded 271-model wall behind the brief's 'deferred_loads=4/4 then hang' (the 4/frame budget only throttle

Fix: Pass allow_sync_model_loads through to drain_render_bridge_submissions instead of hardcoded true; treat non-Menu transitions as 'preloaded or fail-closed', not 'sync-load everything per frame' — i.e., invert the default so render-time loads are cache-hit-only and misses defer to a load queue.

### hang-4 (high)
Texture loads also block the render thread: prime_texture_raw_blocking uses block_in_place+block_on inline, forward pass streams up to 64 blocking primes per frame (forward=233ms contributor)

C++: textureloader.cpp:194-205: dedicated background LoaderThreadClass ('Texture loader thread') performs task->Load() I/O off-thread (:936-962 Thread_Function pops _BackgroundQueue, pushes finished tasks to _ForegroundQueue); main thread TextureLoader::Update (:812-837) only applies completed tasks; failures Apply_Missing_Texture() once (:892-910). W3DDisplay::preloadTextureAssets (W3DDisplay.cpp:3210-3221) funnels through Get_Texture which queues rather than blocks.

Rust: manager.rs:1162-1175 prime_texture_raw_blocking wraps the async archive read in tokio::task::block_in_place + Handle::block_on — called from the render thread. forward_render.rs:526-527 calls stream_pending_textures(texture_stream_budget()) at the start of every ForwardPass::render — budget is 64 when >256 pending (forward_materials.rs:597-611), each iteration doing lock + create_texture_from_cached_assets + blocking prime + decode. forward_render.rs:426-510 prewarm_textures_blocking primes ALL requested textures inline (and drains the queue with budget clamped 64-2048) in a single frame. Textures ARE negatively cached (textures.rs:442-447 cache_missing_fallback → known_missing_textures), so this is bounded unlike the model path — but the synchronous archive reads + DDS/TGA decode on the main thread explain the persistent forward=233ms in the brief.

Fix: Port the C++ split: a background texture-load worker (file read + decode off-thread) with the render thread only uploading finished wgpu textures from a drained queue per frame (the existing pending_texture_stream machinery is already the right shape — remove the blocking prime from the render thread).
close_reason: Menu startup_deferred_model_load_budget never returns 0 (missing startup_frame used to flip allow_sync=true). missing_model_keys negative cache on W3D miss.

title: 271 ShellMapMD models missing: ZH .big files are a delta over base Generals
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### W3D-271-ROOT-CAUSE (high)
271 model_missing root cause: the repo ships only the 17 Zero Hour .big files, which are a DELTA over the base Generals install — every pristine base-game mesh (all trees PT*, civilian props CB*/PM*/CV*, faction units AVPaladin/NVMIG/AVLeopard/UIRGrd_SKN, buildings ABPWRPLANT/NBPwrPlant...) exists in no mounted archive. This is an asset-availability problem, not a path-resolution bug.

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/Win32Device/Common/Win32BIGFileSystem.cpp:31-49 `init()`: `loadBigFilesFromDirectory("", "*.big")` for the ZH run dir, THEN reads base Generals `InstallPath` from the registry and `loadBigFilesFromDirectory(installPath, "*.big")` — retail C++ always mounts the BASE game archives (W3D.big, Textures.big) that carry the shared meshes. ZH-only archives carry just ZH-new/updated art (verified: AVHUMMER.W3D, NVMIGN.W3D, AVTOMAHAWK_MD.W3D exist; pristine AVPaladin/NVMIG/AVTomahawk do not).

Rust: Parsed all 17 BIGs in windows_game/Command & Conquer Generals Zero Hour/ with a BIG index parser: `avpaladin`, `nvmig`, `avtomahawk`, `abpwrplant`, `ptdogwod01`, `ptxpine03`, `uirgrd_skn`, `pmcluster`, `cbquonset1` etc. are in NONE of them (only _d/_md/_n damaged/night/MD variants and .tga/.dds textures exist). Rust already knows: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/assets/archive.rs:192-218 `warn_if_base_archives_missing` logs 'Base Generals archives not loaded (missing: Textures.big, W3D.big)... Zero Hour models may reference textures unavailable in ZH-only archives'. `add_default_search_paths` (archive.rs:46-160) does probe base-install dir names ('Command & Conquer Generals', .../Data, combined layouts, home-sibling scans) — no such install exists in this repo, so nothing mounts. w3d_load_fallback_keys is intentionally empty (mesh_asset_resolve.rs:~530) so no damaged/MD substitution is made.

Fix: Obtain a base Generals install's W3D.big + Textures.big and place them in windows_game/Command & Conquer Generals Zero Hour/ (or point GENERALS_BASE_INSTALL_PATH / GENERALS_ASSETS_DIR at a base install). No code change needed for resolution; the mount order already mirrors C++ (Common/src/common/system/archive_file_system.rs:55-63 loads *.big from every search root).

### hang-271-models-missing (high)
Only 7 render items survived collection (model_missing=271): the ShellMapMD world's objects have no resolvable W3D models, so just 2 roofs + scraps draw

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DDisplay.cpp:1875-1876 `// draw all views of the world; drawViews();` — every Drawable's draw modules render each frame; models are loaded through W3DAssetManager at drawable creation (W3DAssetManager.cpp) with retail .BIG archives mounted, so the shell map's full object set (buildings, props, trees) renders. There is no per-frame budget/skip path that silently drops ~97% of world objects.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/graphics/render_pipeline/pipeline_collect.rs:624-639 `RenderModelLoadResult::Failed => ... model_missing += 1` (also :223, :265, :707 empty-mesh, :738); SkippedByBudget is a separate counter (:616-623), so the live log's model_missing=271 with render_items=7 means 271 objects genuinely failed model resolution/loading, not just budget deferral. Budgets are also tight: startup prewarm caps at 48 (sync) / 12 (async) candidates (pipeline_prewarm.rs prewarm_startup_models `prewarm_limit`), per-frame deferred loads budgeted (pipeline_execute.rs:146-155; live log 0/16 → 4/4 after apply). The 7 surviving items are the "two arched roofs"; the 271 failures are [INFERENCE] unresolved W3D art names against the mounted asset set (not inspected at runtime), consistent with the skybox TGA set also being unresolvable (hang-no-skybox).

Fix: Capture debug_last_missing_model_samples (pipeline_collect.rs:625-638 caps at 16 names) for one live frame and check each name against the mounted .BIG/loose-asset index — the fix is asset-mount/name-resolution coverage (and prewarm seeded from the actual shell-map object list, not a 48-entry cap), not a renderer change.

### W3D-SHELLMAP-EMPTY-WORLD (high)
Yes — this is (the dominant cause of) the empty world: ShellMapMD places 771 objects; 342 are roads/waypoints/scorch decals, 12 ambients and 3 CINE props are skip-listed, and of the remaining 414 model-bearing placements, 334 (81%) reference meshes absent from every mounted BIG. Only 19 templates / 80 placements can actually render.

C++: Retail C++ renders this map fully because the same 334 placements resolve into base-game W3D.big meshes mounted from the registry install path (Win32BIGFileSystem.cpp:37-49).

Rust: Decompressed MapsZH.big:Maps/ShellMapMD/ShellMapMD.map (EAR\0+RefPack, 86,345→1,116,150 bytes CkMp) with a port of script_loader.rs's decoder and counted ObjectsList v3: 771 placements / 108 templates. Cross-checked each template's INI model (135 INI files parsed from extracted INIZH) against the union of all 17 BIGs: missing = 71 templates / 334 spawnable placements, incl. ALL trees (TreeSpruce03×10→PTXPine03, TreeDogwood2×33→PTDogwod02, TreeFir02×28→PTXFIR02, TreeMaple1×23→PTMaple01, ...), rocks, fences (ChainLinkFence×36→PMWallChn2), docks, drums, and even pristine faction units (AVPaladin, NVMIG, ABPWRPLANT, AVComanche, AVTomahawk). Available (ZH-delta art only): TreePalm1×28 (PTPalm01), GLATrap×16 (NBWall), RocksG*, AVHUMMER×4, ZH-new units (Lazr_Crusader/ChinaTankECM/Helix), etc. The observed 271 sits between the distinct-missing (71) and placement-weighted (334) bounds — it is the

Fix: Treat 271 as a symptom metric, not a bug to chase: with base-game archives mounted it collapses toward zero. Optionally add a boot log summarizing 'map X: N placements dropped for unavailable meshes' so the empty-world cause is visible without debug samples.
close_reason: Cannot ship missing base Generals .big files. Fail-soft: reskin ModelName lookup + negative cache + Menu never unbounded-sync. Remaining: retail base assets still required for 271 meshes.

title: Terrain pass clears backbuffer to peach fog; scene skips C++ black clear
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hang-peach-clear (critical)
Terrain pass clears the whole backbuffer to map fog color [0.9,0.71,0.6]; main scene pass then skips its black clear — the screen's base color is peach, not black

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DDisplay.cpp:1640 W3DDisplay::draw; :1859 `WW3D::Begin_Render( true, true, Vector3( 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f ), TheWaterTransparency->m_minWaterOpacity )` — every frame clears BLACK, then :1876 drawViews() paints skybox+terrain over it. Signature GeneralsMD/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/ww3d.cpp:708 `WW3D::Begin_Render(bool clear,bool clearz,const Vector3 & color,...)`, default color Vector3(0,0,0) (ww3d.h:115). No C++ path ever clears to a lighting/fog color (also :1585 Vector3(0,0,0)).

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/graphics/render_pipeline/pipeline_minimap.rs:73-97 `terrain_clear_color()` returns `fog_color.or(ambient_color).or(sun_color)` as the clear color (fog first → ShellMapMD lighting [0.9,0.71,0.6] = the observed peach). pipeline_prewarm.rs:335-437 `update_and_enqueue_terrain_pass` enqueues a pre-scene render pass labeled "main terrain pass" whose color attachment is `load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(clear_color)` (:397, :412) — it is the FIRST pass to touch the backbuffer each frame (called every execute frame, pipeline_execute.rs:283-285). Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/crates/ww3d-renderer-3d/src/rendering/wgpu_main_renderer.rs:413-428: when `had_pre_scene_callbacks` the main scene `render_frame` gets `None` instead of `Some(clear_color)`, i.e. LoadOp::Load — the engine's own black clear (config default Vec4(0,0,0,1), :41) is suppressed exactly when terrain exists. Net

Fix: Make the terrain pass clear opaque black to match W3DDisplay::draw:1859 (or better, leave the terrain pass on LoadOp::Load and let the engine's Begin_Render-equivalent clear black once per frame, restoring the C++ clear-then-draw order). The GENERALS_DEBUG_CLEAR_COLOR env override at pipeline_minimap.rs:74 shows the color was chosen for debugging, not C++ parity. Fog color belongs in the terrain fragment fog blend, never in a clear.
close_reason: terrain_clear_color is wgpu::Color::BLACK matching W3DDisplay.cpp:1859 Begin_Render black clear. Fog no longer paints the backbuffer.

title: Menu→Menu after shell apply destroys MainMenu WND (root_windows=0)
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### HM-1 (high)
Menu→Menu re-transition tears down the shell; C++ never tears down MainMenu when GAME_SHELL finishes

C++: GameLogic.cpp:2195-2203 `if(m_gameMode == GAME_SHELL){ if(TheShell->getScreenCount()==0) TheShell->push("Menus/MainMenu.wnd"); else if(TheShell->top()){TheShell->top()->hide(FALSE); TheShell->top()->bringForward();} HideControlBar(); }` — no hideShell, no MainMenuShutdown. hideShell is explicitly guarded OFF for shell games: GameLogicDispatch.cpp:316-317 `if(!TheGameLogic->isInShellGame()) TheShell->hideShell();`; GameLogic.cpp:2209 `// TheShell->hideShell();` commented out.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/cnc_game_engine/input.rs:906-909 — exit arm `GameState::Menu => { debug!("Exiting Menu state"); self.hide_shell_menu(); }` runs even when new_state==Menu. Trigger chain: boot starts Loading with worker (boot.rs:337-341); slow worker (≥8s @ ≥18%, shell.rs:2001-2018) releases Loading→Menu #1 (camera_drain.rs:452-461) which pushes MainMenu.wnd + MainMenuInit; worker later completes → host_finalize_startup_map_load logs 'Loaded startup shell map' (shell.rs:1891) → fallback_to_menu → transition_to_state(Menu) (shell.rs:1946) = Menu→Menu with full teardown.

Alternative C++-faithful restore: re-enter an already-hidden stack top through Shell::showShell(true) so run_init (MainMenuInit) re-runs.

### HM-2 (high)
Exact teardown chain that blanks the menu: hideShell(immediate) → MainMenuShutdown → layout.hide(true) on ALL windows

C++: MainMenu.cpp:337-347 static shutdownComplete: `isShuttingDown = FALSE; layout->hide(TRUE); TheShell->shutdownComplete(layout);` — C++ WindowLayout::hide (WindowLayout.cpp:56-73) iterates m_windowList which holds ROOT windows only (WindowLayout.cpp:206-210 load adds only info.windows; MainMenu.wnd has one root MainMenuParent), so hideShell hides one root and children inherit invisibility through the hierarchy.

Rust: input.rs:908 → shell.rs:429-441 hide_shell_menu → base.rs:2593-2611 Shell::hide_shell (clear_background=true; run_shutdown(&mut immediate_pop=true); IME detach; is_shell_active=false) → main_menu.rs:814-853 MainMenuShutdown popImmediate branch → main_menu.rs:2101-2110 finish_shutdown_complete: `layout.hide(true)` + is_shutting_down=false (TheShell->shutdownComplete omitted) → layout.rs:65-75 ManagerWindowLayout::hide queues manager.hide_window(win,true) for EVERY window (Rust layout list includes children — layout_load.rs adds recursively) → hierarchy.rs:284-292 hide_window + window_hiding (hierarchy.rs:366-408: keyboard_focus=None, mouse_capture released, modal popped). base.rs:258-261 sets BasicWindowLayout.state=Destroying. Layout is NOT popped — screen_count stays 1.

Fix: Either drop the exit-arm hide entirely for Menu→Menu (preferred, HM-1), or restore via showShell(true) re-init. Structural: make ManagerWindowLayout::hide touch root windows only (C++ layout membership) so per-child HIDDEN state survives.

### HM-3 (high)
Re-enter restores window bits but NOT what MainMenuInit owns — hybrid of two C++ paths, matches neither

C++: Every C++ path that does hideShell re-enters via showShell(TRUE): Shell.h:112 `void showShell( Bool runInit = TRUE );` → Shell.cpp:385-420 `if(runInit){ top()->runInit(NULL); }`; callers PopupSaveLoad.cpp:398, FileTransfer.cpp:257, GameClient.cpp:555 (after intro). MainMenuInit restores focus: MainMenu.cpp:650-651 `layout->bringForward(); TheWindowManager->winSetFocus(parentMainMenu);`, fade cadence and dropdown resets.

Rust: shell.rs:391-394 `else if let Some(top) = shell.top() { top.hide(false); top.bring_forward(); }` — only clears HIDDEN bits + reorders. MainMenuInit (main_menu.rs:591+) never re-runs: no winSetFocus(parentMainMenu) equivalent, no justEntered fade cadence, no dropdown reset, no init-hide-pack reapplication. Consequences: (a) keyboard focus/mouse capture destroyed by window_hiding during teardown and never restored; (b) menu_world_frames_rendered is NOT reset by the real transition (only the test harness resets it, types.rs:220), so the one-shot first-run reveal at input.rs:1201 (`== 45` exact match, reveal_main_menu_first_input_like_cpp → winHide(FALSE) DROPDOWN_MAIN) cannot re-fire — if the worker finalize landed around/before frame 45 (menu frames stall 220ms-1.4s per the WND overlay rebuild), MapBorder2 (parent of ALL menu buttons — main_menu.rs tests 3983-4098 place ButtonSinglePlayer/

Fix: Re-enter through run_init (showShell(true) semantics) whenever the shell was torn down, or eliminate the teardown (HM-1). Reset menu_world_frames_rendered (or re-arm the reveal) on Menu enter.

### wnd-f1 (critical)
Rust GameClient::reset destroys ALL WND windows via WindowManagerSubsystem::reset — C++ GameClient::reset never touches the window manager (no TheWindowManager->reset() caller exists in retail)

C++: GameClient.cpp:426-457 GameClient::reset() resets drawables, TheDisplay, TerrainVisual, RayEffects, VideoPlayer, Eva, SnowManager ONLY — window manager untouched. Grep of entire GeneralsMD/Code for 'TheWindowManager->reset' returns ZERO callers. Window destruction in retail happens only via Shell::doPop→WindowLayout::destroyWindows (Shell.cpp:609-645), Shell::reset, or ~GameWindowManager. MainMenuShutdown (MainMenu.cpp:658-690) never destroys windows: it latches isShuttingDown, cancels patch check, reverse-animates, then shutdownComplete hides the layout. So shell MainMenu.wnd windows survive every game start/load in C++.

Rust: core/game_client/impl_init.rs:142-181 GameClient::reset() → self.subsystem_manager.reset_all() → core/game_client/subsystem.rs:69-74 resets window_manager → core/subsystems.rs:1241-1251 WindowManagerSubsystem::reset → gui/window_manager/mod.rs:341-357 WindowManager::reset → destroy_all_windows() (create_destroy.rs:143-157 drains root_windows, immediately destroys) + layouts.clear() + transitions.reset(). Live triggers of Common GameEngine::reset → game_client.reset(): Common/src/system/SaveGame/game_state.rs:663-666 (every save-game load) and gui/callbacks/popup_save_load.rs:1010-1020 (WND save/load popup load-failure path: engine.reset() then queue_shell_show(true)). This wipes MainMenu.wnd (and every shell layout) from the WM.

If a WM clear is ever needed, it must be paired with Shell stack teardown + re-push like C++ Shell::reset + startNewGame GAME_SHELL push (GameLogic.cpp:2195-2203).

### wnd-f2 (critical)
After windows are destroyed, the Shell stack's stale BasicWindowLayout never recreates them — ensure_layout() short-circuits on the surviving Rc; hide(false)/bring_forward/run_init all no-op, leaving draw_all permanently empty

C++: C++ WindowLayout is destroyed together with its windows: Shell::doPop (Shell.cpp:609-645) unlinks AND deletes the layout object; any later shell screen comes from a fresh winCreateLayout + load(.wnd) in doPush (Shell.cpp:583-607). There is no state where a live Shell stack entry references destroyed windows. GameLogic::startNewGame GAME_SHELL branch (GameLogic.cpp:2195-2203) re-pushes 'Menus/MainMenu.wnd' when screenCount==0, else re-shows the intact top.

Rust: gui/shell/base.rs:211-224 BasicWindowLayout::ensure_layout returns early when self.layout is Some — it never re-runs create_layout_with_windows even after WindowManager::reset cleared the WM registry and destroy_window_immediate (window_manager/create_destroy.rs:209-260) marked every window DESTROYED, removed it from root_windows/window_by_id AND from the owning layout's own list (lines 248-254). So the still-on-stack BasicWindowLayout("Menus/MainMenu.wnd") holds layout=Some(empty Rc): run_init runs MainMenuInit callbacks whose find_window_by_name lookups all fail, hide(false)/bring_forward iterate an empty window list. Main's show_shell_menu (cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:389-393) sees get_screen_count()==1 → else-branch top.hide(false)+bring_forward() → nothing recreated; draw_all iterates root_windows (gui/window_manager/draw.rs:40-46) which is empty.

Fix: Either (a) prevent the destroy (wnd-f1 fix), or (b) make ensure_layout() detect the destroyed state (WM layouts registry no longer contains this layout after reset cleared it) and re-create via create_layout_with_windows, mirroring C++ where the layout object dies with its windows.

### wnd-f4 (medium)
Live Menu re-entry never re-runs MainMenuInit: Main show_shell_menu's stack-non-empty branch only hide(false)+bring_forward, while C++ Shell::showShell(TRUE) re-runs layout->runInit → MainMenuInit (dropdown re-hide, scheme reload, focus)

C++: Shell.cpp:385-446 Shell::showShell(runInit=TRUE): 'layout->runInit(NULL)' re-executes MainMenuInit (MainMenu.cpp:429-653): re-hides dropDownWindows[1..] (all dropdowns incl. DROPDOWN_MAIN/MapBorder2 that contains SOLO PLAY), initialHide(), showSelectiveButtons(SHOW_NONE), layout->hide(FALSE) (line ~579), loadScheme("MainMenu"), bringForward(), winSetFocus(parentMainMenu). WindowLayout::hide (WindowLayout.cpp:56-73) sets winHide on every window and latches m_hidden; runInit is inline in WindowLayout.h:93. GameLogic.cpp:2199-2203 uses the hide(FALSE)+bringForward variant only for the in-game→shell branch — both C++ entry points exist.

Rust: Rust Shell::show_shell(run_init=true) (base.rs:2551-2577) faithfully ports showShell incl. run_init on the top layout, but the live Menu-state entry path never calls it: input.rs:931-956 transition_to_state(Menu) → self.show_shell_menu() (cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:364-426), which does Shell init + show_shell_map(true) + {count==0 → push | else top.hide(false)+top.bring_forward()} — no run_init. ### wnd-f5 (medium)
Observable symptom chain answering 'is draw_all empty': flush_ui_to_frame sees root_windows=0 → zero draw commands → UI render pass skipped → 3D shell-map terrain with no SOLO PLAY/buttons; the 45-frame fallback reveal cannot heal destroyed windows

C++: C++ ordering is correct and always repaints: W3DDisplay.cpp:1863-1867 draws the 3D scene, then TheInGameUI->draw() — which ends with TheWindowManager->winRepaint() (W3DInGameUI.cpp:415) — before End_Render. winRepaint (GameWindowManager.cpp:1309-1340) walks the intact window list in BELOW/normal/ABOVE tail-to-head passes every frame; retail never reaches a shell-active state with destroyed windows.

Rust: Render order parity confirmed (not the bug): Main/src/graphics/render_pipeline/forward_render.rs:670-672 enqueues flush_ui_to_frame as a post-frame callback after the scene; ui_render_pass.rs:147-190 reads root_window_count, calls draw_all, and on had_draw_commands==0 logs 'flush_ui_to_frame: zero draw commands (root_windows=N) — gadget draws queued nothing', ends the frame and returns Ok — no UI render pass at all. draw_all (gui/window_manager/draw.rs:40-77) iterates root_windows only (correct winRepaint port incl. hidden-subtree suppression). After wnd-f1/f2 destruction root_windows is permanently 0. Main's mitigation — input.rs:1198-1203 'staring at terrain with no chrome, reveal after ~1.5s' → reveal_main_menu_first_input_like_cpp → reveal_hidden_main_menu (main_menu.rs:650-662) — only flips not_shown and unhides MapBorder2 via find_window_by_name, which returns None for destroyed wi

Fix: Fix the root causes (wnd-f1/f2/f3) rather than the symptom. Diagnostic aid: the existing 'zero draw commands (root_windows=N)' log plus the Shell top-filename residual (dispatch.rs:793-797) lets a smoke test assert root_windows>0 whenever GameState::Menu has a non-empty shell stack.

title: Five-flag sit-through blocked: no WND, never InGame, status file starved
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hq-9e2w-flag-wnd-nav-dead (critical)
After this hang, wnd_widget_tree_nav can never latch — the physical-input latch chain needs a pumping winit loop AND a started offline match; the session had neither before death

C++: Win32GameEngine.cpp:106-160 — Win32GameEngine::update() calls serviceWindowsOS() every engine update; PeekMessage/GetMessage/TranslateMessage/DispatchMessage at :118-155 keeps OS mouse input flowing even while the shell map runs. SelectionXlat.cpp:141 — TheWindowManager->getWindowUnderCursor(c2.x, c2.y) is the retail widget-tree nav, fed by that pump. GameLogic.cpp:2197-2198 — GameLogic::startNewGame pushes Menus/MainMenu.wnd and returns to the pump, so menu nav never wedges the message loop.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/cnc_game_engine/input.rs:247-253 — only OS WindowEvent::MouseInput maps to MouseInputOrigin::Physical; input.rs:368-383 — note_menu_wnd_click/note_skirmish_path_gadget require Physical origin + GameState::Menu + enabled gadget hit; types.rs:580-583,665-667 — match_started_from_menu_wnd (set only from host_start_game_from_ui, start_game.rs:406-407) is the third conjunct of wnd_menu_to_match_complete. Hang session: stayed Menu the whole time (camera_drain.rs:1337-1343 'Menu NewGame drain: ignore GAME_SHELL'; brief log 'worked — stayed Menu'), so match_started_from_menu_wnd was false at hang onset; after onset the single winit event-loop closure (run_loop.rs:560-703) never returned (macOS 'not responding'), so no WindowEvent::MouseInput can ever reach handle_mouse_button_input; process exited 1. All three conjuncts are permanently false.

Fix: Root cause sits with the menu re-enter/hang scouts; for the sit-through itself, wnd_widget_tree_nav cannot recover without (a) the event loop returning to the pump between frames and (b) a real offline match start from a physical skirmish-path gadget click. Do not soften the Physical-origin gate (input.rs:374-375) to work around the hang.

### hq-9e2w-flag-ingame-dead (critical)
InGame flag can never latch this session — engine never left GameState::Menu (GAME_SHELL drained as ignore) and the observer never saw any status

C++: Shell.cpp:448-466 (GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GUI/Shell/Shell.cpp) — Shell::showShellMap issues MSG_NEW_GAME with GAME_SHELL for the shell map only (m_pendingFile = m_shellMapName); it is not a match start, matching the Rust drain-ignore. GameLogic.cpp:2197-2198 — shell menu push returns to the pump; retail transitions to a real game only via a user-driven start.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/executable_smoke.rs:210-213,1432-1440 — reached_ingame latches only from a parsed status snapshot with state=InGame|Paused and a non-shell map; start_game.rs:179-184 and camera_drain.rs:1337-1343 — GAME_SHELL is deliberately ignored (shell map, not a match), and the brief shows the NewGame drain kept the session in Menu; the process died exit=1 while still in Menu. Additionally the status file /tmp/generals_windowed_status.txt stayed 0 bytes, so parse_status (executable_smoke.rs:519-522) returned None every poll — even a hypothetical InGame frame would have been unobservable.

Fix: No flag-side change: InGame is honestly false. Unblockers are the menu re-enter hang and match-start path owned by other beads; the status-starvation finding below must also be fixed or any later InGame transition is invisible to the harness.

### hq-9e2w-flag-gameplay-dead (critical)
interactive_gameplay can never latch — strictly downstream of the dead menu→match chain (match_started_from_menu_wnd && physical RMB order with selection)

C++: Retail RMB orders flow through the same pumped message stream (Win32GameEngine.cpp:118 PeekMessage each update) into LookAtXlat/CommandXlat; there is no path where a context order latches without the pump delivering the mouse release after a real game start.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/cnc_game_engine/types.rs:669-671 — gameplay_complete() = match_started_from_menu_wnd && gameplay_order; types.rs:585-590 — note_gameplay_order requires windowed && match_started_from_menu_wnd && had_selection; input.rs:436-467 — gameplay_order is noted only on a Physical-origin RMB press→release gesture (no drag) that issued an order in-world. match_started_from_menu_wnd was false at hang onset (stayed Menu) and no Physical input can arrive after onset, so interactive_gameplay is dead by transitivity from the two findings above.

Fix: No independent fix: latch unblocks automatically once a physical menu→match transition completes and InGame is reached. Keep the inject path (input.rs:519+, origin Injected) excluded from this latch.

### hq-9e2w-status-starvation (high)
Status-file starvation makes ALL five flags unobservable in the harness even when internally true — publish only happens at the end of drive_frame or after a drained host command, and an empty file parses as nothing

C++: No C++ counterpart (five-flag honesty gate is a Rust-harness construct); nearest retail analog is Win32GameEngine.cpp:106-160 where the pump runs every update, so no single wedged subsystem silences all observation channels.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/cnc_game_engine/run_loop.rs:95-98,283-284 — publish_status runs only after each drained runtime-host command or as the LAST step of drive_frame; any hang inside apply_runtime_host_command / engine.update / engine.render freezes the last published status forever (this hang: 0 bytes from first write). executable_smoke.rs:519-522 — parse_status returns None on empty text, so saw_window_visible/saw_live_frame_ok/saw_wnd_widget_tree_nav/saw_interactive_gameplay (executable_smoke.rs:1317-1330) never set and the five-flag report shows all false regardless of internal engine state. runtime.rs:222-231 — without -runtime_host + gpui_* args no bridge exists and nothing is ever published; note the /tmp/generals_windowed_status.txt path appears nowhere in the repo, so an external launcher created it empty.

Fix: Diagnostics only (do not soften honesty): verify future launches pass -runtime_host=windowed -gpui_status=... so publish_booting (run_loop.rs:76-78) ever runs; keep parse_status fail-closed.

### hq-9e2w-flag-liveframe-bridge-gated (medium)
live_frame_ok and window_visible are NOT blocked by this hang itself, but live_frame_ok can never latch in a bridge-less windowed launch — the present-latch call is gated on the RuntimeHostBridge existing

C++: No direct counterpart: retail always has a DX8/WW3D device presenting frames whenever a window exists; visibility and presentation are not conditional on an external control harness.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/cnc_game_engine/run_loop.rs:176-183 — note_windowed_surface_presented() is only called inside 'if let Some(bridge) = runtime_host_bridge.as_mut()'; runtime.rs:199-206 sets has_published_live_frame there; runtime.rs:445-451 — published live_frame_ok = capture-promoted OR has_published_live_frame. Frames WERE presented before the hang (brief: 'terrain=51ms forward=233ms render_items=7', matching the breakdown logged from graphics/render_pipeline/pipeline_execute.rs:325-326), and the window was visible (dispatch.rs:586-590 window_visible_from_winit_query on the live winit query; no 'window_visible stays false' warning from run_loop.rs:314-322/411-416 fired). So both flags were internally satisfiable pre-hang — only the status channel hid them. But if this launch omitted -runtime_host (consistent with a permanently 0-byte status file), live_frame_ok could never lat

Fix: For future sit-through attempts: always launch with -runtime_host=windowed plus -gpui_status/-gpui_control/-gpui_frame so the honest present-latch and visibility residuals can be published. Do not move the latch out of the bridge gating — that would let plain launches self-certify live_frame_ok.
close_reason: Named blockers fixed live: gpui-status now 1372 bytes (hyphen flags), WND tree present (ButtonSinglePlayer hittable), process pumping. InGame/gameplay still require physical sit-through (hq-9e2w). playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

title: GPU terrain ignores BlendTileData; source tiles never uploaded
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### terrain-gpu-ignores-map-tiles (high)
Live GPU terrain never uses the map's BlendTileData — ground is procedurally textured by height/slope, not by map tiles

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/WorldHeightMap.cpp:1043-1141 ParseBlendTileData reads per-cell m_tileNdxes/m_blendTileNdxes/m_extraBlendTileNdxes and texture classes, then immediately loads tile bitmaps via readTexClass (999-1037: TheTerrainTypes->findTerrain(name) -> TERRAIN_TGA_DIR_PATH+texture -> readTiles into m_sourceTiles). updateTileTexturePositions (1443-1560) packs source tiles into texture pages (m_tileLocationInTexture with TILE_OFFSET gutters). getUVForNdx (1589-1623) returns the per-tile UV rect (quadrant-selected for half tiles) and is used per cell corner at 1707-1780 (U[4]/V[4] writes). TerrainTex.cpp:199-310 + updateFlat (343) CPU-bake blended tile pixels into the D3D terrain texture; W3DTerrainBackground.cpp:171/564/716-723 consume getFlatTexture (WorldHeightMap.cpp:2205). Every ground cell shows the map's own authored tile art.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/terrain/terrain_visual/impl_gpu.rs:186-196 — per-vertex weights come from texture_system.generate_texture_weights(height, slope, tex_coords, &self.texture_rules) (textures.rs:1195), a procedural height/slope rule engine. texture_rules come from ensure_default_textures (impl_lighting.rs:286-341): at most one texture per surface Grass/Rock/Snow/Sand from Terrain.ini with hardcoded height/slope profiles (base_rule_for, impl_lighting.rs:398-437). Chunk UVs are chunk-normalized: chunk.rs:232-235 tex_u=x/(resolution-1), tex_v=z/(resolution-1) spanning the whole 128-unit chunk (CHUNK_SIZE, chunk.rs:54), never per-cell tile UVs. src/shaders/terrain.wgsl:56-70 samples the 4 bound whole-file TGAs at those stretched UVs. The map's tile_ndxes/blend_tile_ndxes never reach update_chunk_meshes, select_stable_chunk_texture_ids (impl_gpu.rs:300-347 picks textur

Fix: Wire the already-parsed per-cell tile data into the GPU path: either (a) port the C++ CPU bake — pack source_tiles into per-draw-area atlas textures (updateTileTexturePositions analog) and emit per-cell UVs from tile_ndxes via a getUVForNdx analog in chunk generate_geometry, or (b) reuse the existing but test-only HeightMap::get_pointer_to_tile_data (height_map.rs:823) to bake per-chunk wgpu textures. Replace generate_texture_weights blending with tile-authored blending.

### terrain-source-tiles-dead-on-gpu (high)
Decoded map source tiles are loaded into memory but never uploaded or sampled by any GPU pass

C++: WorldHeightMap.cpp:1122/1135 readTexClass fills m_sourceTiles/m_edgeTiles during map parse; 1461-1514 assigns each tile a location in the terrain texture; 2529-2531 and getPointerToTileData (2387) feed blended pixel data into TerrainTextureClass baking, which becomes the visible ground.

(add_object_selection.rs:1321-1331), whose comment explicitly says 'do not run a second parallel ScriptEngine::update loop here' — which scripts_camera.rs:378 does anyway. crate update_active -> execute_side_scripts walks every side's root+groups (update.rs:177-260) gated only by crate player_list().count(); when the crate PlayerList is non-empty every condition/action (SET_MILLISECOND_TIMER, MOVE_CAMERA_TO, SET_FLAG, CALL_SUBROUTINE 'Loud'/'Soft'/'Run Drop') can execut

description:

### hq-scr-1 (high)
Shell scripts DO smash the camera: MOVE_CAMERA_TO drives focus to world y=0 (ground/void), matching the peach-void screenshot

C++: C++ ScriptEngine::setTimer with millisecondTimer=true treats the parameter as SECONDS: 'm_counters[counterNdx].value = REAL_TO_INT_CEIL(ConvertDurationFromMsecsToFrames(value*1000))' (ScriptEngine.cpp:6726-6731), so ShellMapMD 'Move Camera' arms a 3600-frame countdown and 'If at 0..120' fire MOVE_CAMERA_TO(CAM_n,10s) every 300 frames. In C++ the waypoint Coord3D (x,y_map,z=0) is a ground-plane location handed to TheTacticalView; the eye height stays owned by the view's zoom/pitch, so the camera never dives. GameLogic::update runs TheScriptEngine->UPDATE() with no GAME_SHELL gate (GameLogic.cpp:3598-3601). [Exact doCameraMoveToWaypoint line not quoted; camera-height ownership inferred from TacticalView contract]

Rust: Decoded from the retail map (windows_game/extracted_big_files/MapsZH/Maps/ShellMapMD/ShellMapMD.map, RefPack-decompressed, 82 scripts confirmed): 13 one-shot scripts 'If at 0..120' gated on COUNTER(Restart Camera)==3599..1 each do MOVE_CAMERA_TO(CAM_n,10,0,0,0) + CAMERA_MOD_LOOK_TOWARD(LookAt_n). Waypoints parsed from the same map: CAM_0=(987.9,357.4,z=0) ... InitialCameraPosition=(827.9,234.3,z=0) — all z=0. Live chain: executor/actions_player_display_camera.rs:285-295 resolves the waypoint and passes (x, y_map, z=0) through; MissionScriptActionHandler::move_camera_to converts via camera_coord3d_to_world = Vec3::new(x, z, y) (mission_scripts.rs:293-296) -> world height = z = 0.0; ScriptCameraMoveTo lerps start.lerp(target) with target = request.position (script_camera.rs:78-97), sinking the focus from terrain height (~28) to y=0 over 10s; scripts_camera.rs:1317-1340 update_script_camera

Fix: Clamp/derive the script camera focus height from terrain ground height at (x,z) when applying MOVE_CAMERA_TO/waypoint camera requests (C++ semantic: waypoint supplies ground-plane XZ only; view keeps height), e.g. sample terrain height in camera_coord3d_to_world consumers or in ScriptCameraMoveTo::new before lerp.

title: TreeSpruce03 looked up as W3D name; C++ uses ObjectReskin ModelName
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### W3D-TREE-SPRUCE-MODEL (medium)
'TreeSpruce03.w3d not in any BIG' is expected: TreeSpruce03 is an INI object name (ObjectReskin of GenericOptTree); its actual mesh is ModelName = PTXPine03 (NatureProp.ini), and PTXPine03.w3d also ships only in the base game. A bare 'TreeSpruce03' model request happens only through object-name-as-model-key fallbacks.

C++: C++ resolves the drawable through ThingTemplate → W3DTreeDraw/W3DModelDraw ModelName (PTXPine03) and asks the AssetManager for art/w3d/ptxpine03.w3d across ALL mounted BIGs (ZH run dir + base install + mods). It never asks for TreeSpruce03.w3d. MapsZH.big carries the map/preview only (verified: 299 entries, 0 .w3d) — the claim 'C++ loads from art/w3d or MapsZH' is half right: art/w3d inside the mounted BIG union, not MapsZH.

Rust: windows_game/extracted_big_files/INIZH/Data/INI/Object/NatureProp.ini:2856-2860 `ObjectReskin TreeSpruce03 GenericOptTree` → `ModelName = PTXPine03`. PTXPine03.w3d is in no BIG; only Art/Terrain/PTXPine03.tga (TerrainZH.big) and a mention in Art/W3D/Models.txt — a manifest INSIDE W3DZH.big that lists the full cross-archive art set (incl. base-game names), not that BIG's contents. Rust mostly follows C++ (Main ini_parser.rs:1303 'model|modelname|w3dmodel' captures ModelName; model_cache object→model), but object-name fallbacks exist: mesh_asset_resolve.rs:783-788 `model_key_from_presentation` (empty model_key → template_name), model_key_from_template (empty get_model_name → template.name), and manager.rs:prewarm_object_models_blocking `get_model_for_object(name).unwrap_or_else(|| name.to_string())` — any of these emits a TreeSpruce03.w3d lookup that can never succeed.

Fix: Nothing to fix in path construction. If you want the samples legible, ensure prewarm/collect sites log the INI-resolved model (PTXPine03) rather than falling back to the object name; the real fix is the missing base-game archives (see W3D-271-ROOT-CAUSE).
close_reason: TreeSpruce03 lookup uses reskin ModelName PTXPine03. tree_spruce03_lookup_uses_reskin_modelname pass.

title: Terrain shader distance-fogs every fragment to fog_color (peach world)
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hang-terrain-fog-always (high)
Rust terrain shader unconditionally distance-fogs every fragment to fog_color — with the high shell camera most terrain renders as flat peach, indistinguishable from the clear; C++ scene fog is disabled by default

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/scene.cpp:69-72 SceneClass ctor: `FogEnabled(false), FogColor(0,0,0), FogStart(0.0f), FogEnd(1000.0f)`; W3DScene.cpp:931 `DX8Wrapper::Set_Fog(FogEnabled, FogColor, FogStart, FogEnd)` merely forwards those defaults — no Generals game code ever calls Set_Fog_Enable/Set_Fog_Range on the RTS3DScene (grep over GameEngineDevice returns no setters). C++ terrain is never fog-filled to the lighting color; the horizon is skybox or black clear.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/terrain/shaders/terrain.wgsl:110-112 `let fog_factor = clamp((distance_to_camera - uniforms.fog_start)/(uniforms.fog_end - uniforms.fog_start),0,1); final_color = mix(final_color, uniforms.fog_color, fog_factor);` — applied unconditionally in fs_main; beyond fog_end every terrain pixel equals fog_color (the peach). Fog values come from map metadata via set_lighting (impl_lighting.rs:81-84; world_env.rs:514-518, defaults fog_start=800/fog_end=3000 impl_core.rs:73-75) — with the logged shell camera at height ~350 (pos (870,349.77,351), focus (870,28.26,770), ~528 units to focus), all far terrain converges to the same peach as the clear, which is why the frame reads as a uniform peach void even after chunks exist.

Fix: Gate the terrain fog on the scene-fog flag like C++ (FogEnabled=false default → no fog blend), or source fog from the same GlobalData/TOD lighting records C++ uses for its (disabled) scene fog. Fog must be a state, not an unconditional shader constant; the acceptance answer for "peach not ShellMapMD world" is: peach clear (hang-peach-clear) + no skybox (hang-no-skybox) + fog-blended terrain (this) all rendering the same lighting triple.
close_reason: terrain.wgsl only mixes fog_color when fog_end>fog_start. Live fog_range=None no longer flattens the mesh to peach.

title: Shell skybox never binds: TSMorning TGA missing, all-or-nothing abort
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hang-no-skybox (high)
Skybox is silently skipped when its 5 TGA textures fail to load — sky region keeps the peach clear; C++ draws a real skybox mesh asset whenever DrawSkyBox is on

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Water/W3DWater.cpp:1071 `m_skyBox = ...Create_Render_Obj( "new_skybox", TheGlobalData->m_skyBoxScale, 0)`; :1702-1707 in WaterRenderObjClass::Render (:1499): `if (TheGlobalData && TheGlobalData->m_drawSkyBox) { pos=rinfo.Camera.Get_Position(); pos.Z=m_skyBoxPositionZ; m_skyBox->Set_Position(pos); m_skyBox->Render(rinfo); }` — a world mesh from the asset manager (textures swappable per map, replaceSkyboxTexture :1301). Enabled per map via INI key DrawSkyBox (GlobalData.cpp:154), default FALSE (GlobalData.cpp:656).

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/terrain/terrain_visual/impl_gpu.rs:615-621 `record_skybox_background_draw` early-returns with no log when `skybox_background_bind_group` is None. The bind group only exists if ≥1 skybox texture loaded: impl_world.rs:726-732 `refresh_skybox_background_binding` sets bind group None when no `skybox_textures[i]` is Some; textures come only from `replace_skybox_textures` → `load_skybox_replacement_textures` → `load_texture_from_path` → `load_runtime_texture_image(path)?` (impl_world.rs:621-657, 669-683) which hard-errors when the TGA is not in mounted assets. Caller pipeline_minimap.rs:194-213 catches the Err and merely debug!-logs "Skipping default skybox texture override because mounted assets do not expose the legacy fallback set" (DEFAULT_SKYBOX_TEXTURES = TSMorningN/E/S/W/T.tga, render_pipeline/mod.rs:676-680) — exactly the live-hang condition,

Fix: Mirror C++ materially: resolve the "new_skybox" mesh asset (or at minimum keep a procedural sky gradient) instead of silently returning; log at warn! when an explicit map skybox hint fails to load. Also honor C++ default m_drawSkyBox=FALSE (GlobalData.cpp:656) rather than defaulting skybox_enabled=true (pipeline_lifecycle.rs:38) so parity is opt-in per map like retail.

### SKYBOX-1 (high)
Skybox is NOT bound after the apply: the default TSMorning*.tga set does not exist anywhere in the mounted asset set, so replace_skybox_textures always errors on the default (skirmish) path and the peach clear remains

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Include/GameClient/Water.h:85-89 — WaterTransparencySetting defaults m_skyboxTextureN..T = "TSMorningN.tga"…"TSMorningT.tga"; these TGAs ship in base-Generals Textures.big (ZH requires the base game installed). W3DWater.cpp:1071 creates the skybox render obj; W3DWater.cpp:1702 draws it gated on TheGlobalData->m_drawSkyBox.

Rust: Main/src/graphics/render_pipeline/mod.rs:676-682 DEFAULT_SKYBOX_TEXTURES = TSMorning{N,E,S,W,T}.tga. Authoritative parse of windows_game/Command & Conquer Generals Zero Hour/TexturesZH.big (3546 entries, header 0x10 + offset/size/NUL-name per the game's own big_file_system.rs:234-294 parser): ZERO entries matching 'morning'; only tsmoonsky_*.dds, tsrain_*.dds, tsblizzard_*.dds, tsavalanch_*.dds. Glob of both extracted trees (extracted_big_files*/TexturesZH/Art/Textures): no tsmorning files. Glob windows_game/**/*.big: only ZH archives — no base-game Textures.big/W3D.big exists to supply them. load_skybox_replacement_textures (GameClient/src/terrain/terrain_visual/impl_world.rs:669-684) therefore returns Err('runtime texture TSMorningN.tga not found') and replace_skybox_textures propagates it before any binding; pipeline_minimap.rs:325-336 logs only debug ("Skipping default skybox texture

Fix: Point DEFAULT_SKYBOX_TEXTURES at a set that exists in TexturesZH.big (e.g. tsmoonsky_{n,e,s,t,w}.dds or tsrain_*.dds), or fall back per-face instead of erroring when the legacy set is absent. Findings only — not implemented.

### SKYBOX-2 (high)
All-or-nothing texture load: the ? in replace_skybox_textures aborts before the bind-group refresh, so even 4-of-5 available faces bind nothing

C++: W3DTerrainVisual::replaceSkyboxTextures (W3DTerrainVisual.cpp:1135-1152) replaces textures per index independently; one bad texture never blocks the others or the default mesh.

Rust: impl_world.rs:646 'let loaded_textures = self.load_skybox_replacement_textures(&replacements)?;' — the ? fires BEFORE refresh_skybox_background_binding_if_ready() (line 655). load_skybox_replacement_textures maps Results and collects (impl_world.rs:676-682), so any single missing texture fails all five. First call seeds current names to "" (lines 626-632) so all five always enter replacements on a fresh visual. Net: one missing asset = zero bound textures = no draw.

Fix: Filter replacements to resolvable textures and bind the remainder (C++ per-index semantics), calling refresh_skybox_background_binding even on partial failure. Findings only — not implemented.

### SKYBOX-3 (high)
Explicit map skybox hints also cannot resolve: runtime_texture_candidates does no .tga→.dds swap and no map-directory search, while every map-provided name exists only as .dds

C++: W3DTerrainVisual.cpp:1135 + W3DWater.cpp:1301-1310 resolve map-supplied names through the W3D asset manager, which retries DDS-then-TGA and searches all mounted archives including the map's own files (retail ZH ships these sky faces as DDS inside TexturesZH.big, exactly as this repo's archive shows).

Rust: Only 3 maps in MapsZH define SkyboxTextureN/E/S/W/T: MD_USA04 + MD_USA04_CINE use 'TSMoonSky_N.tga…' and USA05_EndsConflict_INTRO_N uses 'TSRain_N.tga…' (extracted_big_files*/MapsZH/Maps/*/Map.ini). TexturesZH.big holds these only as art/textures/tsmoonsky_n.dds and tsrain_n.dds — no .tga variants. runtime_texture_candidates (impl_world.rs ~878-925) tries only Data/{lang}/Art/Textures/{name}, Art/Textures/{name}, and user-data dirs with the literal extension — no extension swap and no map-mount directory, unlike Main's assets/textures.rs swap_texture_extension path. So even maps with explicit hints can never bind on this path; all skirmish maps fall through to the missing defaults (SKYBOX-1).

Fix: Add a tga→dds candidate (mirroring Main assets/textures.rs swap_texture_extension) and/or map-directory candidates in runtime_texture_candidates. Findings only — not implemented.
close_reason: replace_skybox_textures binds whatever faces load; TGA/DDS + Art/Textures candidates. terrain_visual skybox tests pass.

Rust impl_sleepy.rs:118-176: (a) no cur-module guard — during process_sleepy_updates the entry is POPPED, so awaken finds it 'not in heap' and re-pushes from module_lookup, then the requeue also re-adds it → module scheduled twice → double update per frame; (b) the re-add path takes object_id from entries.first() AFTER retain() filtered (impl_sleepy.rs:150-160) — i.e. an unrelated module's object id, or drops the wake entirely when lookup misses; (c) UpdateSleepTime::Forever drops the entry from the heap (impl_sleepy.rs:74-77) so a module can never be re-woken by the heap itself; (d) no 'awake at now, requested now+1 → keep now' rule, so an awaken can delay a module C++ would have run this frame. Only affects dual-tick builds (crate not live by default), but it is the C++-parity scheduler.

title: ENTER/EXIT condition semantics forked into three inconsistent implementations vs C++'s single 2-frame flag model
description:
**Type:** bug
**Priority:** 1
**Parent:** hq-in69
**Labels:** parity,cpp-vs-rust,script-campaign,high
Subsystem: script-campaign (compare verdict mostly, score 58)
Severity: high
C++: Object::didEnterOrExit; Team::didAllEnter/didPartialEnter (whichToConsider filter)
Rust: eval_named_entered_area (eval_named.rs:559), evaluate_named_entered_area_condition (eval_area.rs:203), Team::object_did_enter (team_areas.rs:122), eval_team_entered_area_entirely (eval_basic.rs:1693)
allowed_if_wgpu: False
C++ has ONE model: Object::didEnterOrExit() returns true if m_enteredOrExitedFrame == now || == now-1 (Object.cpp:2467-2478, comment explains ScriptEngine-before-ObjectUpdates ordering), flags cleared on next-frame position change (Object.cpp:2351-2365). Rust has three divergent semantics for the same C++ conditions: (1) executor live path eval_named_entered_area uses a LATCH: entered = last_enter_frame > condition.custom_frame (eval_named.rs:559-585) — a unit that entered while a script was disabled still triggers NAMED_ENTERED_AREA when the script re-enables; C++ would not (window closed). title: KindOf is encoded five different ways; no layer uses the retail 116-bit layout completely, and the Common template layer truncates to u64
description:
**Type:** bug
**Priority:** 1
**Parent:** hq-in69
**Labels:** parity,cpp-vs-rust,common-ini-xfer-kindof,critical
Subsystem: common-ini-xfer-kindof (compare verdict diverges, score 55)
Severity: critical
C++: KindOfType / KindOfMaskType = BitFlags<116> (KindOf.h:81)
Rust: KindOfMask(u128) + ThingTemplate.kindof(u64) + Main KindOf enum + core.rs KindOfMaskType + selection_xlat KINDOF_* u32
allowed_if_wgpu: False
C++ retail (ALLOW_SURRENDER never #defined anywhere in GeneralsMD — verified by grep) has KINDOF_COUNT=116; LINEBUILD=15, ALWAYS_SELECTABLE=1<<53 (KindOf.h:38-73, KindOf.cpp name list). Rust Common kind_of.rs:15-135 is a u128 with PRISON=15/COLLECTS_PRISON_BOUNTY=16/POW_TRUCK=17/CAN_SURRENDER=44 — every bit >= LINEBUILD is +4 vs retail (ALWAYS_SELECTABLE=1<<57). Save semantics survive because masks serialize by NAME (BitFlagsIO.h:157-224, Xfer.cpp:658-693; Rust xfer.rs:757 does the same). BUT ThingTemplate stores `kindof: u64` (thing_template.rs:1407) via `self.kindof = mask.bits() as u64` (thing_template.rs:2842): u128 bits 64-119 (= retail bits 60-115) are silently dropped — FS_TECHNOLOGY..IGNORE_DOCKING_BONES incl. HERO, INERT, SUPPLY_SOURCE, POWERED, DRONE, BALLISTIC_MISSILE, NO_SELECT, BOAT, PARACHUTE, HULK, DEMOTRAP, and 11 of the 14 KINDOFMASK_FS members (all except FS_FACTORY=62/FS_BASE_DEFENSE=63) vanish from the live template mask. `KindOfMaskType = u64` alias at thing.rs:21-22. Additionally the Main live host uses a hand-curated `enum KindOf` with NON-C++ members (Resource, Worker, Attackable, Harvestable — host_types.rs:74-143) and Main/src/core.rs:126-188 defines a retail-correct u64 KindOfMaskType that stops at FORCEATTACKABLE=1<<63 ('More bits would require additional handling') and is referenced nowhere else. GameClient selection_xlat.rs:161-178 adds a sixth local u32 encoding (KINDOF_ALWAYS_SELECTABLE=0x4) packed from kind NAMES via catalog_kind_of_flags — a UI-local cache, internally consistent, but another parallel definition that can drift.
Acceptance:
- [ ] Live path matches C++ observable behavior for this finding
- [ ] Verified against cited C++ symbols, not crate-only / test-only code
close_reason: Retail KindOf.h ALLOW_SURRENDER-off layout is now default: KindOfMask ALWAYS_SELECTABLE=53 FORCEATTACKABLE=63 KINDOF_COUNT=116; ThingTemplate.kindof stores KindOfMask.bits() as u128 so bits>=64 survive (C++ KindOfType / KindOfMaskType BitFlags<116>).

description:

Rust: Weapon::reload_with_bonus / apply_post_fire_state / Weapon::update
allowed_if_wgpu: False
C++ Weapon::reloadWithBonus (Weapon.cpp:1877-1917): (1) early-returns when clipSize>0 && ammo==clipSize && !isReloadTimeShared() so a reload never restarts inappropriately; (2) refills ammo immediately (0 → 0x7fffffff = unlimited); (3) when isReloadTimeShared() syncs every other slot's whenWeCanFireAgain + RELOADING_CLIP; (4) rebuildScatterTargets(). title: Restore supply-center collector autopilot and remove fabricated passive income
description:
C++ uses an event-driven collector economy, not periodic player income. SupplyCenterProductionExitUpdate::exitObjectViaDoor first follows the authored exit path and then calls SupplyTruckAIInterface::setForceWantingState(true) for every SupplyCenter output (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/ProductionExitUpdate/SupplyCenterProductionExitUpdate.cpp:101-111). The forced wanting state selects a legal source or center and docks at authored cadence (SupplyTruckAIUpdate.cpp:459-530; AIDock.cpp:551-612). Money is credited only on the SupplyCenter dock action: the center controlling player drains carried boxes, adds the upgrade boost, calls Money::deposit, and records money earned (SupplyCenterDockUpdate.cpp:77-89). ActionManager::canTransferSuppliesAt requires the transfer destination controlling player equal the truck controlling player (ActionManager.cpp:224-230); warehouse pickup only transfers one box/depletes stock and grants no money (SupplyWarehouseDockUpdate.cpp:69-115). There is no global passive-income path in C++.

Active Main has a real Gathering -> ReturningResources -> credit_supplies route (GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/support_states.rs:3305-3565), but it is not entered by normal SupplyCenter creation or production: one-shot collector creation sets only producer/orientation (world_objects/create_destroy_die.rs:57-135) and paid completion does the same (world_tick/production.rs:942-1028); Object::new starts Idle. The spawn-ready path only supplies generic movement (world_tick/production.rs:1035-1163). The active template parser retains only Queue/DefaultProductionExitUpdate and drops SupplyCenterProductionExitUpdate (world_objects/spawn_templates.rs:1081-1225), despite the dormant GameLogic port already representing the C++ handoff (GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/supply_center_production_exit_behavior.rs:174-187).

Meanwhile every normal Main tick calls update_player_resources (world_tick/step.rs:950-953), fabricating $5/sec per player and $25/sec per constructed SupplyCenter (world_objects/resources_income.rs:80-141). This coexists with live deposits: combat_particles_and_economy.rs:3041-3175 creates a ReturningResources carrier, observes SupplyDropoffEvent, and explicitly accepts the passive residual at 3135-3141. That fabricated tick grants money/statistics/economy logs without a collector, source, cargo, or dock event and masks the missing automatic collector route.

Implement one source-authored SupplyCenterProductionExit metadata/exit handoff for both one-shot and paid outputs; only eligible supply trucks from that producer must enter the actual gather route after the C++ authored exit timing. Preserve exact controlling-player (not merely team) source/center selection and deposit ownership. Then remove $5/$25 fabricated supply credit while retaining real power handling/economy authority. Do not touch GameNetwork or WGPU, and do not wire dormant GameLogic wholesale into Main.

Focused regressions: (1) no manual command: a center-produced collector acquires a finite warehouse, returns, and creates one exact deposit after its action cadence; no money changes before deposit; (2) a paid collector output takes the same route while a non-SupplyCenter harvester output does not; (3) advancing frames with no collector, empty/dead source, or destroyed collector leaves supplies/resources_collected/economy events unchanged; (4) two players on one team cannot use or credit the other player center; (5) save/load mid-gather and mid-return resumes source target, cargo, preferred center/autopilot state without duplicate free collector or synthetic income. C++ saves SupplyTruckAI state, preferred dock, carried boxes, and force state (SupplyTruckAIUpdate.cpp:242-255), so active Main snapshot coverage must retain equivalent live state.

Existing unrelated snapshot_restore_rebuilds_state_and_object_id_counter failure remains outside collector scope.

title: Fix HTree column-major parent/local matrix composition
description: Discovered from hq-7s9. Main assets/models.rs mat4_mul is documented and consumed as glam column-major (Mat4::from_cols_array/to_cols_array), but indexes as row-major: for column-major inputs it returns B*A. Thus compute_htree_global_transforms_from_locals_with_capture_controls calls mat4_mul(parent, local) yet produces local*parent, contrary to C++ HTreeClass::Base_Update/Anim_Update Matrix3D::Multiply(parent->Transform, pivot->BaseTransform) and Capture_Update postMul control (GeneralsMD WW3D2/htree.cpp:478-552, pivot.cpp:97-130; WWMath matrix3d.h:32-45, matrix3d.cpp:583-637). Noncommuting proof: source parent Rz(+90) and child Tx(2) must yield source (0,2,0), render basis (0,0,2); current helper yields source/render (2,0,0). Correct free helper to actual column-major A*B, route loader duplicate mat4_from_tr_quat through the canonical correctly column-major mat4_from_pivot (it currently transposes rotations), and remove/align dead duplicate mat4_mul. Add noncommuting hierarchy/capture/basis regression tests. Affects rigid HLOD bind/animation, capture controls, turret/recoil, skin palette, aggregates, and non-HLOD pivot-name loader fallback.
notes: Implemented the exact column-major C++ Matrix3D parent/local order in Main's shared HTree evaluator.  now computes source affine lhs*rhs, preserving Matrix3D::Multiply(parent, local) and Capture_Bone postMul control semantics; the duplicate HMODEL pivot builder now delegates to canonical mat4_from_pivot so it cannot transpose quaternion rotation independently. Added a noncommuting Rz90 parent + Tx child regression that proves source child (0,2,0), capture postmultiply inheritance (0,5,0), and loader HMODEL residual parity. Green: cargo test -p generals_main --lib assets::models::tests::htree_source_matrix_multiply_keeps_cxx_parent_local_and_capture_order -- --exact --test-threads=1 (1 passed, 8035 filtered).

title: Correct W3D HTree source matrix composition order
description: Discovered from hq-7s9. GeneralsMD Matrix3D::Multiply(parent, local) is column-vector parent*local (matrix3d.cpp:570+; Transform_Vector in matrix3d.h:1677-79); Main assets/models.rs mat4_from_pivot produces that same source matrix in glam column-major form, but mat4_mul currently computes b*a. A parent Rz90 plus local Tx2 stays +X instead of rotating to +Y, corrupting HTree globals, Capture_Bone controls, HLOD rigid children, palettes, and HMODEL residuals. Replace with explicit correct column-major source multiplication, unify the duplicate W3DLoader matrix builder if safe, and add noncommuting parent/local + control regressions. No GameNetwork.
notes: Superseded by hq-418, which implemented and verified the same column-major HTree parent/local composition correction. No duplicate work remains.
close_reason: Duplicate of hq-418

title: Correct W3D HRaw animation local delta composition
description: Discovered while implementing hq-oi6. GeneralsMD HTreeClass::Anim_Update computes parent * BaseTransform then post-multiplies the sampled translation and quaternion delta (htree.cpp:519-545; Matrix3D::Translate matrix3d.h:592-620). Main sample_animation_local_transforms currently overwrites base local translation components and rotation for flags 0/1/2/6 in Code/Main/src/assets/models.rs, so animated pivots diverge whenever authored bind pose is nonidentity/rotated. Port exact local post-composition/interpolation behavior (including raw Generals frame wrapping semantics) with base transform retained; test translated/rotated bind pivots and descendants. Coordinate with hq-oi6 index normalization; no GameNetwork.
notes: Implemented C++ Generals raw HAnim sampling in assets/models.rs. Raw W3D animation now selects one integer frame using C++ Float_To_Long nearest-even semantics, wraps frames at NumFrames, applies BaseTransform then local translation delta then quaternion delta, uses identity outside channel ranges, does not normalize raw quaternions, ignores pivot-zero raw channels, and keeps final duplicate X/Y/Z/Q source channels exactly as HRawAnimClass::add_channel does. Raw visibility uses the same specialized rounded/wrapped frame. Existing compressed animation interpolation remains isolated. Green focused regressions: raw_hanim_uses_cxx_integer_delta_postcomposition_and_duplicate_channel_rules, pre30_hierarchy_and_raw_animation_insert_and_address_the_synthetic_root, htree_runtime_pose_ignores_authored_pivot_zero_pose_channels_and_visibility, bridge_capture_controls_apply_to_the_same_gpu_palette_as_rigid_hlod_children, and multi_lod_rigid_hlod_uses_cxx_constructor_selection_and_retains_attachment_metadata; all passed individually. hq-418 separately fixed the prerequisite column-major HTree parent/local multiplication and passed its focused regression.
close_reason: Exact raw HAnim delta composition, frame selection, visibility, and duplicate-channel behavior implemented with focused regressions green

No GameNetwork.

title: Model C++ WW3D render-object prototype registry
description: Discovered from hq-at9. Aggregate attachment rendering cannot safely load and draw a whole file or use aliases/placeholders. Port a source-backed immutable prototype registry/strict resolver with full-name lookup, file-stem load-on-demand, and only exact prototype output; missing prototype returns None. Coordinate with hq-at9 for recursive HLOD AdditionalModels. No GameNetwork.

title: Preserve C++ known-zero Drawable barrel-count semantics
description: Discovered during hq-pi6 v4 snapshot/barrel review. Acceptance: an authored ShotsPerBarrel=3 slot fires twice under validated zero topology and each post-shot state has cursor 0/shots_left 2; after transition to a valid two-barrel topology, subsequent fire follows the C++ prefire and postfire sequence; snapshot/restore while zero topology preserves that state.

WeaponBarrelState preserves zero and mirrors the C++ prefire guard by resetting cursor and ShotsPerBarrel cadence before every zero-topology shot. Added focused regression for ShotsPerBarrel=3, two zero-topology shots, then transition to two barrels.
