title: Persist transactional shroud/FOW state across staged save restore
description: Discovered from hq-pi6 v4 snapshot review. C++ persists fog-of-war in the logic snapshot: PartitionCell::xfer writes m_shroudLevel[MAX_PLAYER_COUNT] (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/PartitionManager.cpp:1485-1500), and PartitionManager::xfer serializes every cell plus m_pendingUndoShroudReveals and refreshes local shroud on load (lines 4558-4645). Active Main WorldSnapshot has no shroud payload. Worse, host staged load mutates process-global shroud before commit: CnCGameEngine::stage_saved_world_for_restore in Main/src/cnc_game_engine/host_authority.rs creates staged GameLogic then calls staged.load_map; GameLogic::load_map_with_progress initializes get_shroud_manager().lock().init_shroud_grid(world_width, world_height) (Main/src/game_logic/world_save.rs:2120-2122) and load-map completion invokes update_main_crate_vision, revealing map-spawned staging objects. SnapshotBuilder::restore_from_snapshot replaces staged objects but never restores the singleton; host_replace_game_logic only swaps GameLogic and clears renderer state. Successful loads therefore leak staging-map visibility into the saved world; any future stage failure after map load can also leave the still-active old GameLogic paired with staged global FOW. Implement an explicit shroud snapshot of persistent per-cell player levels and pending undo reveals, and a transaction boundary: staging must not mutate the live singleton, or the singleton must be fully snapshotted/restored on failure and atomically install the loaded shroud only with successful host world replacement. Do not rebuild only from restored object vision: that loses explored/fog and queued temporary reveals, unlike C++. Map exact APIs: GameLogic::load_map_with_progress; GameLogic::update_main_crate_vision in Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/spawn_templates.rs; gamelogic::system::shroud_manager::{get_shroud_manager, ShroudManager::init_shroud_grid, clear_all, do_shroud_reveal, queue_undo_shroud_reveal}; host_authority::{stage_saved_world_for_restore, host_replace_game_logic}. Acceptance: (1) save/load preserves hidden/explored/visible per-cell FOW and pending reveal expiry, (2) successful stage cannot retain map-start staging reveals, (3) injected staged-load failure leaves active GameLogic and global shroud unchanged, (4) integration test covers a same-map load with differing save-time FOW.
notes:
Static API map and minimal boundary: ShroudManager owns private Option<ShroudGrid> with width, height, cell_size, and Vec<PartitionCell>. Each PartitionCell owns CellShroudLevel[MAX_PLAYER_COUNT], whose full state is current_shroud plus active_shroud_level. SightingInfo is where_pos, how_far, for_whom, expiration_frame in pending_undo_shroud_reveals. Existing public snapshot_grid_for_player returns only derived Hidden/Explored/Visible bytes and is insufficient: C++ ShroudLevel Xfers both counters in Display.h lines 18-22, so overlapping lookers or active shrouders would be lost. Add a narrow GameLogic-side ShroudSnapshot and ShroudManager snapshot_state/replace_state that preserve grid dimensions, full per-cell levels, undo queue, and pre-grid full/permanent reveal queues if retained; visible/explored object sets are caches and should rebuild after install. Smallest safe host transaction without broad singleton removal: capture old singleton before stage_saved_world_for_restore, use an RAII rollback guard across map load plus snapshot restore, return staged ShroudSnapshot with staged GameLogic, restore old singleton before returning, then extend host_replace_game_logic or adjacent single host boundary to install staged logic and shroud together. This prevents success and error leaks. Snapshot schema needs an explicit new world tail/version plus exact bincode predecessor/direct-Xfer gate; do not encode a presentation-only grid.
Source audit follow-up: staged restore mutates more process-global gameplay state than ShroudManager. stage_saved_world_for_restore calls staged.load_map; fast/legacy map sync resets and loads gamelogic terrain singleton in Main/src/game_logic/world_save.rs around 1280-1283 and 1432-1435, replaces ThePlayerList around 1533-1535, and resets/rebuilds get_team_factory around 1554-1605. A later snapshot error therefore leaves active GameLogic paired with staged terrain/player/team globals; successful restore also retains map-default globals unless snapshot/commit owns them. Treat these singleton mutations as part of the same stage transaction: either isolate map loading from active singleton state or capture/restore all affected global state on failure and atomically commit the staged set after snapshot success. NamedObjectTracker is additionally mutated only for Shell map objects, so it is lower-priority for offline mission/skirmish but should be audited with the same boundary.

Forced post-restore failure regression preserves terrain/player/team/sides/shroud/script/named/area/AI/integration globals plus all queue state. title: show_shell_menu idempotence depends on shell_menu_active bookkeeping
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### HM-5 (medium)
show_shell_menu idempotence guard makes the Menu→Menu enter depend solely on shell_menu_active bookkeeping

C++: Shell::showShellMap (Shell.cpp:448-466): returns early when already in GAME_SHELL — same no-op. Shell::showShell (Shell.cpp:385-420) is the init re-run entry (Shell.h:112 default runInit=TRUE).

Rust: shell.rs:364-427: guard `if self.shell_menu_active { return; }` is the only skip; after Menu→Menu it is false (reset at shell.rs:440), so re-enter always runs init+show_shell_map(true)+unhide. base.rs:2761-2764 show_shell_map early-returns once host_replace_game_logic installed the GAME_SHELL instance (matches C++). If the first enter failed mid-push (shell.rs:416-425 error paths), shell_menu_active stays false and the menu may never have been fully initialized — the Menu→Menu then 're-enters' a stack top whose windows were never created.

Fix: Track shell_menu_active against actual shell teardown (hideShell ran), or key the enter-arm work off is_shell_active rather than a host-side boolean.
close_reason: show_shell_menu inspects live shell.get_screen_count()/top(), not stale shell_menu_active.

title: DeclineResolution calls shell.reset(); C++ just pushes MainMenu.wnd
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### wnd-f3 (high)
MainMenu::decline_resolution calls shell.reset() + show_shell(true) — C++ DeclineResolution unconditionally pushes Menus/MainMenu.wnd; Rust show_shell only pushes when shell map is OFF, so with retail shell map ON the stack stays empty after resolution decline

C++: MainMenu.cpp:714-752 DeclineResolution(): reverts display mode, writes Options.ini, then 'delete TheShell; TheShell = NULL; TheShell = MSGNEW(...) Shell; TheShell->init(); ... TheShell->push( AsciiString("Menus/MainMenu.wnd") );' — an explicit, unconditional push. It never calls showShell.

Rust: gui/shell/main_menu.rs:2178-2182: queue_shell_operation(|shell| { let _ = shell.reset(); let _ = shell.show_shell(true); }). Shell::reset (base.rs:2893-2901) pops all screens via pop_immediate → destroy_windows (all shell windows destroyed, stack emptied). Shell::show_shell (base.rs:2551-2577) pushes 'Menus/MainMenu.wnd' only when !global.shell_map_on && stack empty. Main's show_shell_menu already called shell.show_shell_map(true) (cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:388) and base.rs:2790 sets self.shell_map_on=true, so the push is skipped → empty stack → blank menu until GameState::Menu is left and re-entered (input.rs:931-956 → show_shell_menu pushes because count==0). Wrong C++ counterpart: showShell is a different function than the push DeclineResolution uses.

Fix: Replace shell.show_shell(true) with shell.push("Menus/MainMenu.wnd", false) after shell.reset() to match C++ DeclineResolution line-for-line.
close_reason: DeclineResolution pushes Menus/MainMenu.wnd after Shell init. decline_resolution_pushes_main_menu_wnd_like_cpp pass.

### hang-tile-texture-fallback (medium)

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/TerrainTex.cpp:64-170 `TerrainTextureClass::update(WorldHeightMap *htMap)` copies the map's authored tile pixel data (`pTile->m_tileLocationInTexture`, :101-129) into the terrain texture atlas — tile imagery ships inside the .map, so C++ terrain is textured even with no loose terrain .tga files, with 4-pixel borders against seams (:60-62).

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/terrain/terrain_visual/impl_gpu.rs:663-671 `prepare_chunk_texture_binding` substitutes `fallback_texture_id` (first registered texture) or 0 when a tile texture id is unregistered; :708-726 texture id 0 (or failed diffuse load) acquires a solid-color texture from `DEFAULT_TERRAIN_COLORS` via `create_solid_texture` (textures.rs:1052-1106). Default texture set comes from INI Terrain types on disk gated by `is_available_terrain_texture_path` (impl_lighting.rs:288-343). Result: chunks whose authored tiles aren't mounted render as flat colored patches — the screenshot's "white scraps" — then get fog-blended toward peach (hang-terrain-fog-always).

Fix: Parse the .map's embedded tile bitmaps (WorldHeightMap tile data) into the chunk texture atlas like TerrainTex.cpp:64 instead of requiring loose INI-registered .tga files; keep the solid-color path only as an explicit logged fallback.
close_reason: DEFAULT_TERRAIN_COLORS missing slot is dark gray [80,80,80], not snow-white [240,240,240].

title: Extra-blend pass samples procedural slot-0, not extra-blend tile art
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### terrain-extra-blend-overlay-wrong-texture (medium)
Extra-blend second pass samples the procedural chunk slot-0 texture, not extra-blend tile art, so it cannot reproduce C++ 3-way blends

C++: WorldHeightMap getExtraAlphaUVData + the W3D second pass composite the third tile's pixels with per-corner alpha over the base terrain (driven by m_blendedTiles orientation, m_extraBlendTileNdxes, and alpha tile data).

Rust: impl_gpu.rs:941-953 extra_blend_mesh_to_terrain_vertices hardcodes blend_weights=[1.0,0,0,0]; record_extra_blend_pass (impl_gpu.rs:1029-1074) binds chunk_texture_bindings.values().next() — the procedural chunk bind group — and samples it at get_extra_alpha_uv_data UVs. With blended_tiles empty (see parser finding), get_extra_alpha_uv_data (height_map.rs:618-669) returns default data with all-zero corner alphas for every extra-blend cell, so the C++ 3-way blend art cannot appear even geometrically correct.

Fix: Give the extra-blend overlay its own bind group over the packed source-tile atlas with UVs from the extra blend tile index, and drive corner alpha from parsed blended_tiles records; until tiles are GPU-resident, suppress the overlay rather than drawing wrong-texture quads.
close_reason: extra_blend_mesh_to_terrain_vertices uses blend slot 1, not slot-0 procedural.

title: Shell camera uses (870,770) fallback; ignores InitialCameraPosition waypoint
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### CAM-1 (medium)
(870,770) is a hardcoded shell-camera fallback equal to C++ W3DView::init's pre-lookAt default — retail never shows this view because GameLogic::startNewGame overrides it with the InitialCameraPosition waypoint lookAt

C++: W3DView.cpp:609-625 W3DView::init(): 'pos.x = 87.0f; pos.y = 77.0f; pos.z = 0; pos.x *= MAP_XY_FACTOR; pos.y *= MAP_XY_FACTOR; setPosition(&pos);' — init-time default lookAt (870,770). GameLogic.cpp:2014-2032 then overrides: startingCamName = keyToName(TheKey_InitialCameraPosition); 'Waypoint *way = findNamedWaypoint(startingCamName); if (way) { Coord3D pos = *way->getLocation(); TheTacticalView->lookAt(&pos); }' (else fallback pos={50,50,0}), followed by initHeightForMap/setAngleAndPitchToDefault/setZoomToDefault (GameLogic.cpp:2033-2037). The shell game (GAME_SHELL via Shell::showShellMap) goes through this same startNewGame camera block.

Rust: Main/src/cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:817-832 select_startup_camera_focus(): shell branch returns 'metadata_target.unwrap_or(Vec2::new(87.0 * gamelogic::common::MAP_XY_FACTOR, 77.0 * gamelogic::common::MAP_XY_FACTOR))' = (870,770) (MAP_XY_FACTOR=10, Common map_object.rs:11). Comment itself admits: 'C++ shell startup prefers InitialCameraPosition and only falls back to the legacy W3DView seed when the waypoint is absent.' Observed log target (870,28.26,770) is exactly this seed. Live-path true: bootstrap call sites shell.rs:1923-1930 and start_game.rs:441-447 both pass is_shell_game from presentation shell-bypass.

Fix: Wire the already-parsed waypoint into the shell bootstrap so metadata_initial_camera is Some on shell boot: in the startup map-load finalize (host_finalize_startup_map_load / complete path before bootstrap_camera_for_loaded_map), call game_logic.queue_pending_camera_focus(waypoint) or extend PresentationFrame build (presentation_frame/build.rs:1541) to fall back to the map's initial_camera_position when peek_pending_camera_focus() is None. select_startup_camera_focus already prefers metadata (co

### CAM-2 (medium)
raw_initial=None because live bootstrap reads the script-camera request queue (pres.camera_focus = peek_pending_camera_focus), while the parsed InitialCameraPosition metadata (meta.initial_camera_position) has zero live consumers

C++: C++ uses the actual waypoint from loaded map data: GameLogic.cpp:2015-2032 findNamedWaypoint(TheTerrainLogic waypoints) + TheTacticalView->lookAt; MapUtil.cpp:301-305 and INIMapCache.cpp:92,121 also parse InitialCameraPosition into m_waypoints.

Rust: shell.rs:856-861: metadata_initial_camera = pres.camera_focus (presentation freeze only). presentation_frame/build.rs:1541: 'camera_focus: logic.peek_pending_camera_focus().map(...)' — this is the host's pending script/radar camera request queue (eva_camera.rs:706-708), set only via request_camera_focus (eva_camera.rs:493-501) from scripts/cheats/radar — never seeded at shell boot. Meanwhile script_loader.rs:1005 does parse the waypoint: 'meta.initial_camera_position = parse_initial_camera_position_from_chunky(chunky)...' and the parser (script_loader.rs:1682-1759) correctly handles the v3 waypoint-dict form — verified against retail ShellMapMD bytes it returns Some((827.89, 234.29, 0)). But grep shows the only consumer of initial_camera_position in Main is debug binary bin/inspect_shell_map.rs:149; position_camera_from_map (GameLogic game_start.rs:386-392) and get_initial_camera_positio

Fix: Minimal change: at shell-map load finalize, push meta.initial_camera_position into the host queue (queue_pending_camera_focus) BEFORE the presentation freeze is built, so existing plumbing (build.rs:1541 → shell.rs:856) picks it up with no renderer changes.

### CAM-4 (medium)
Parity gap confirmed: retail shell view is the InitialCameraPosition waypoint at world (827.9, 234.3) — about 536 world units (~54 tiles) north of the Rust fallback — and no scripted camera move exists in the map to reconcile them

C++: GameLogic.cpp:2029-2032 lookAt(waypoint->getLocation()) is the retail shell-menu camera start; waypoint located in map data at (827.89, 234.29, 0) (verified by parsing the retail ObjectsList: object '*Waypoints/Waypoint' at x=827.888 y=234.291 with dict waypointName='InitialCameraPosition'). The decompressed map contains no PlayerScriptsList chunk and zero occurrences of 'MoveCameraTo' — no scripted pan overrides the initial view, so the waypoint lookAt IS the retail menu backdrop framing.

Rust: Live shell camera aims at (870,770) instead of (827.9,234.3): a ~536-unit north-south offset. Content differs too: waypoint area is a flat plateau (9x9 raw heights 28-29, only 7 objects within 300 units) while the fallback hovers the dense battle cluster (116 objects within 300). So the Rust menu backdrop shows the map-center fight, not the authored quiet north-area view C++ frames. Both are inside playable [0,1750]^2, so this is a framing/parity gap, not an empty-terrain bug.

Fix: Same wiring as CAM-1/CAM-2; expected post-fix log: raw_initial=Some((827.89, 234.29, 0)) with target x/z = (827.9, 234.3). Note InitialCameraPosition y is the map's ground-plane second axis (C++ z is height, =0 here); Rust Y-up conversion must map it to Vec3::new(x, height, y) — the existing code comment at shell.rs:862 ('InitialCamera.y is height, not a map axis') already encodes the right convention for the metadata path.

### hq-scr-4 (medium)
Live shell startup camera focus does not match the map's InitialCameraPosition waypoint

C++: C++ reads the map's InitialCameraPosition waypoint to seed the shell tactical view at map load (parsed by the Rust loader too: script_loader.rs:1682 parse_initial_camera_position_from_chunky); Generals retail shell shows the scene framed on that waypoint (827.9, 234.3 in ShellMapMD). [Exact C++ seeding line not quoted]

Rust: Decoded map waypoint: InitialCameraPosition=(827.9, 234.3). Live log from the hang session shows the actual startup focus (870, 28.26, 770) — neither coordinate matches. CnCGameEngine::select_startup_camera_focus (cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:817-880) prefers 'shell metadata target' before other seeds, and its own tests (shell.rs:1219-1246) codify metadata-before-seed ordering with no InitialCameraPosition preference, so the retail framing is not reproduced; combined with hq-scr-1 the shell view starts wrong and then dives.

Fix: In select_startup_camera_focus, prefer the map's InitialCameraPosition (metadata.initial_camera_position) for GAME_SHELL ahead of the generic shell metadata target.
close_reason: PresentationWorldEnv.initial_camera_position seeded from map metadata. Bootstrap prefers it over script camera_focus queue.

description: Late fidelity finding AFTER plan handoff — did not go through Round 2/3. C++ KindOf.h has KINDOF_CAN_ATTACK, KINDOF_FORCEATTACKABLE, KINDOF_ALWAYS_SELECTABLE. Rust kind_of.rs may be missing them. Verify enum order/bits before adding.

notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-15 HEAD=1df030242 — STALE-PREMISE / already present. Closing.

kind_of.rs is not missing CAN_ATTACK, FORCEATTACKABLE, or ALWAYS_SELECTABLE. All three (and SHRUBBERY / LOW_OVERLAPPABLE) exist at C++ KindOf.h SOURCE-ORDER bit positions. Present since file add fd0795a9b (2026-03-12). Session SHRUBBERY/LOW_OVERLAPPABLE note is also already in-tree.

Side-by-side (KindOf.h source-order vs kind_of.rs):
- CAN_ATTACK: C++ bit 3 = Rust 1<<3 (kind_of.rs:19)
- SHRUBBERY: C++ bit 6 = Rust 1<<6 (kind_of.rs:22)
- ALWAYS_SELECTABLE: C++ bit 57 = Rust 1<<57 (kind_of.rs:73)
- LOW_OVERLAPPABLE: C++ bit 66 = Rust 1<<66 (kind_of.rs:82)
- FORCEATTACKABLE: C++ bit 67 = Rust 1<<67 (kind_of.rs:83)

KIND_OF_BIT_NAMES is a 120-entry exact match of KindOf.h including four ALLOW_SURRENDER names. Rust documents ALLOW_SURRENDER always-on.

Retail compile (ALLOW_SURRENDER undefined, KINDOF_COUNT=116) would shift ALWAYS_SELECTABLE/LOW_OVERLAPPABLE/FORCEATTACKABLE by -4 (53/62/63). That is a known stance (file comment + wave989), NOT "flags missing." Do NOT append. Do NOT reorder. If retail bit alignment is ever wanted, drop/skip the four surrender slots — that is a different M ticket (INI parse, save/load, every mask test).

GameLogic enums.rs KindOf is a semantic enum (not C++ bit layout) and already has CanAttack/AlwaysSelectable/ForceAttackable.
close_reason: STALE-PREMISE: CAN_ATTACK=1<<3, ALWAYS_SELECTABLE=1<<57, FORCEATTACKABLE=1<<67 already in kind_of.rs matching KindOf.h source-order. SHRUBBERY/LOW_OVERLAPPABLE also present. Do not add or reorder bits.

title: Shell MUSIC_SET_TRACK handler is a stub; C++ starts shell music
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hq-scr-3 (medium)
Frame-0 shell scripts call MUSIC_SET_TRACK but the live handler is a stub — shell music never starts (and cannot hang)

C++: C++ ScriptEngine::update runs scripts in GAME_SHELL (GameLogic.cpp:3598-3601); ShellMapMD frame-0 scripts 'Set Music' (MUSIC_SET_TRACK Game_USA_1), 'Unshroud' (MUSIC_SET_TRACK Shell), 'Set Initial Audio Vollumn' (MUSIC/SOUND/SPEECH_SET_VOLUME) route through ScriptActions -> TheAudio, starting the looping shell soundtrack.

Rust: MissionScriptActionHandler::music_set_track (mission_scripts.rs:2359-2363) only calls hooks.note_music_started + push_message("Music track: X") — no audio subsystem call. SOUND_SET_VOLUME/SPEECH_SET_VOLUME/MUSIC_SET_VOLUME similarly never reach AudioManagerSubsystem via this handler. Verified against the decoded script dump: these actions fire on the first script tick (CONDITION_TRUE one-shots), i.e., in the same tick that logged 'ScriptEngine first update: named cache populated' before the process died — so audio actions are present at the death tick but are queue-push no-ops, exonerating the script/music path as the hang and confirming a shell-music parity gap.

Fix: Route music_set_track/music_set_volume through the audio subsystem (AudioManagerSubsystem queue_event / music track selection) as C++ TheAudio does; coordinate with the audio slice to avoid double ownership.
close_reason: MissionScriptActionHandler::music_set_track calls TheAudio add_audio_event. music_set_track_queues_named_track_on_the_audio pass.

title: INI readLine deltas: CRC bytes trimmed, no 1028-char split, '=' not a first-token separator
description:
**Type:** task
**Priority:** 3
**Parent:** hq-in69
**Labels:** parity,cpp-vs-rust,common-ini-xfer-kindof,low
Subsystem: common-ini-xfer-kindof (compare verdict diverges, score 55)
Severity: low
C++: INI::readLine / INI::load
Rust: INI::read_line / parse_file / get_first_token
allowed_if_wgpu: False
C++ readLine strips ';' comments, maps control chars (>0 && <32) to spaces, keeps trailing whitespace, and hard-splits lines at INI_MAX_CHARS_PER_LINE=1028 (INI.cpp:392-465); the raw buffer is then CRC-xfer'd (INI.cpp:458-463). Rust read_line truncates at ';', trims, replaces only '\t', has no length cap, then CRCs the TRIMMED buffer (ini.rs:1231-1280) — CRC differs from C++ whenever trailing whitespace exists. get_first_token uses split_whitespace; C++ strtok uses m_seps=" \n\r\t=" so a block header containing '=' tokenizes differently. s_xfer CRC is only wired for a fixed GameData.ini path list (Main/src/subsystem_manager.rs:336-340, config/global_data.rs:776-777); full network INI CRC is GameNetwork territory (deferred_ok).
Acceptance:
- [ ] Live path matches C++ observable behavior for this finding
- [ ] Verified against cited C++ symbols, not crate-only / test-only code
close_reason: INI::read_line now strips ';' comments, maps control chars to spaces, keeps trailing whitespace, hard-caps at INI_MAX_CHARS_PER_LINE=1028, and CRCs the raw buffer (C++ INI::readLine INI.cpp:397-464).

Monitor target size after full main test rebuild; install cargo-sweep if it creeps past ~10GB.
